items.summary: The Election Commission will share machine-readable ('readable PDF') draft and final electoral rolls — soft copies, plus addition/deletion/modification supplements — with recognised political parties for the first time, a reversal after years of refusing the demand citing privacy/fudging concerns and a 2018 Supreme Court order that backed its stance. Congress (@INCIndia, Oct 16 X post) claimed the concession as a victory for Rahul Gandhi's long-running demand, saying the ECI had finally 'bowed'. Commentator Mohit Chauhan asked whether the ECI will also release the pre-SIR machine-readable rolls, noting SIR risks burying evidence of earlier deletions.
items.title: ECI to share 'readable' (machine-readable) voter rolls with parties for the first time; Congress claims victory
